meta.description: Prepare, audit, or revise Nature-ready Data Availability statements, data repository plans, dataset citations, and FAIR metadata checklists for manuscripts. Supports Chinese-to-English data availability wording and bilingual operation for Nature-family submissions.

scientific_integrity.detail: Does not invent DOIs, accession numbers, or identifiers. Flags 'available upon request' as weak. Requires explicit dataset-to-location mapping.

practice_boundaries.detail: Appropriate scope for data availability statement preparation. Enforces Nature/Springer Nature data-sharing policies. FAIR principles aligned with community standards.

methodological_ground.detail: Access route classification (public/controlled/third-party/restricted) follows established data governance. Repository selection hierarchy is evidence-based (DOI > accession > stable URL).

code_usability.detail: Clear 8-step workflow with ready-to-paste output format. References include statement patterns and checklist templates.

functional_suitability.note: Complete data availability workflow: dataset inventory, access route classification, repository selection, statement drafting, dataset citation, FAIR audit. Handles auditing existing statements and preparing new ones.

reliability.note: Strong quality gates: no invented identifiers, explicit dataset-to-location mapping required, FAIR audit before finalization. Flags weak patterns like 'available upon request'. Minor: lacks validation for identifier format correctness.

performance_context.note: Efficient on-demand loading for policy/repository/FAIR references. Core workflow lean. Minor: no guidance for handling very large dataset inventories (100+ datasets).

agent_usability.note: Clear 4-step routing protocol. Manifest-driven always_load. Runtime parameter detection (journal, language, access route) handled inline. Minor: access route classification could use decision tree guidance.

human_usability.note: Excellent bilingual support with 中文核对 block. Ready-to-paste output format. Clear separation of statement text, actions, and missing information. Comprehensive Chinese trigger phrases.

security.note: Does not handle or expose sensitive data directly. Flags restricted/controlled access appropriately. Prompts for ethics approvals and access committees rather than inventing them. No credential leakage risk.

maintainability.note: Excellent modular design. Core stance, Chinese mode, and workflow separated. Policy/repository/FAIR references on-demand. Journal-specific requirements cleanly isolated (nature-article-requirements.md, NMI via nature-shared).

agent_specific.note: Strong parameterized workflow. Inline journal/language detection efficient. Clear 8-step process. Minor: lacks explicit guidance for multi-dataset deduplication. Missing examples of complex access route combinations.

key_strengths: Excellent quality control: no invented identifiers, explicit dataset-to-location mapping required, 'available upon request' flagged as weak
Strong bilingual support with 中文核对 block for Chinese-speaking authors preparing English submissions
Comprehensive access route classification (public/controlled/third-party/restricted/justified-request) with clear guidance
Clean integration of journal-specific requirements (Nature Article mandatory deposition, NMI Code availability section)
Robust FAIR metadata audit covering provenance, license, README, DataCite fields, and file organization

recommendations.title: Add identifier format validation
recommendations.problem: Skill checks for presence of DOIs/accession numbers but doesn't validate format correctness (e.g., DOI regex 10.\d{4,}/\S+, NCBI accession patterns, GitHub release vs commit hash).
recommendations.root_cause: Repository-and-identifiers.md describes identifier hierarchy but lacks format validation rules.
recommendations.fix: Add identifier format validation step before finalizing statement. Include regex patterns for common identifiers (DOI, PMID, GEO accession, PDB ID, GitHub release DOI). Flag format errors in 'Missing information / risk flags' section.

recommendations.title: Add access route decision tree guidance
recommendations.problem: Access route classification (workflow step 3) relies on agent judgment without explicit decision tree. Complex cases (e.g., sensitive data with possible anonymization, third-party data with reuse permissions) lack structured guidance.
recommendations.root_cause: Workflow describes routes but not decision logic for edge cases.
recommendations.fix: Create references/access-route-decision-tree.md with flowchart: Start with data sensitivity → Check legal/ethical restrictions → Evaluate anonymization feasibility → Determine public vs controlled vs restricted. Include examples for common edge cases.

recommendations.title: Prioritize FAIR audit findings (P0/P1/P2)
recommendations.problem: FAIR audit flags missing metadata comprehensively but doesn't prioritize blocking issues (e.g., missing license preventing reuse) vs nice-to-have metadata (e.g., detailed provenance narrative).
recommendations.root_cause: fair-metadata-checklist.md lists checks without severity levels.
recommendations.fix: Add priority levels to FAIR audit: P0 (blocking: license, access conditions), P1 (critical for findability: DOI, title, authors), P2 (enhances reusability: detailed provenance, code comments). Report P0 issues first in 'Missing information / risk flags'.
